title: Inflow and Infiltration Localization for Urban Sewer Networks Using Point of Interest‐Based Hydraulic Model and Pipe Infiltration Likelihood Model
content:
Abstract

Inflow and infiltration (I&I) is a typical issue in separated urban sewer networks (USNs) contributing to treatment plants overloads, combined sewer overflows, urban flooding and other environmental problems. However, the lack of spatio-temporal inflow data from real-time monitoring and field measurements presents a challenge in accurately identifying I&I locations. To address this, this study proposes a novel I&I localization method based on Point of Interest (POI)-based hydraulic model and pipe infiltration likelihood model (PILM), with open-source public databases. Sewer inflows for each manhole are estimated based on connected building discharges from surrounding areas derived from building type and area information obtained from POI database. An optimization approach based on Iterative Local Updating Ensemble Smoother is employed to calibrate a USN dry-weather hydraulic model, determining time-series inflows by using the previously estimated flows as prior information. The calibrated hydraulic model is further integrated with the PILM to estimate and localize I&I flows within the network. The proposed method is applied to a real USN in southern China. Results demonstrate good agreement between simulated and observed sewer flows and water depths under dry-weather conditions, with mean KGE and R 2 values both of 0.94 at flow monitoring locations and 0.92 and 0.86 for the water level monitoring locations. Estimated I&I flows achieve average KGE and R 2 values of 0.79 and 0.82. Field sampling confirms the reliability of the I&I localization results. The proposed I&I estimation and localization method has the potential to enhance USN management and inform related maintenance and rehabilitation efforts.
